title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: A practical Drexel University guide to lounges, study zones, meeting spaces, and outdoor areas with clearly documented shared uses.

cards.title: Bring Lunch Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Couches, work tables, and kitchen equipment in Rush Student Center
cards.notes: The refrigerator and industrial microwave make this a practical pause point for commuter students carrying food, while tables support light study.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused lounge for eating, resting, socializing, or light study.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel says the lounge provides commuter students with couches, tables, chairs, televisions, a refrigerator, and an industrial microwave for socializing or light study.
cards.access_notes: Intended primarily for commuter students; Rush Student Center access and operating rules apply.

cards.title: Reset With Coffee or a Group Session
cards.subtitle: An all-Dragons lounge inside Main Building
cards.notes: Use the open lounge for a study break or informal meeting; private use of its conference area follows a separate reservation process.
cards.short_summary: A shared lounge for studying, relaxing, meetings, television, and complimentary coffee.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel invites all Dragons to use Main 220 for relaxing, studying, group meetings, live television, and complimentary coffee.
cards.access_notes: Drexel says the lounge is open most weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; private conference-space use requires an email reservation.

cards.title: Go Upstairs After the Dining Stop
cards.subtitle: Lounges, games, and study areas share one floor
cards.notes: The second floor lets a group shift between conversation, games, and coursework without treating the first-floor dining area as the only destination.
cards.short_summary: An upstairs mix of student lounges, game rooms, and study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel states that Ross Commons contains student lounges, game rooms, and study areas above its first-floor dining space.
cards.access_notes: Drexel describes Ross Commons as a community space for students, faculty, staff, and guests; current building rules and hours apply.

cards.title: Reconfigure the Room for the Work
cards.subtitle: Movable seating, whiteboards, and presentation equipment near Race Street Walk
cards.notes: Adjust the furniture for solo or group work, or use the documented equipment when a session needs a board or projected display.
cards.short_summary: A flexible study area equipped for individual work, collaboration, tutoring, or coaching.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel says the Library Learning Terrace has adjustable seating, whiteboards, a projector, and a private hub station for tutoring or coaching.
cards.access_notes: Verify current access hours and follow any posted reservation rules; scheduled tutoring or coaching may occupy the private hub.

cards.title: Move a Campus Gathering Outdoors
cards.subtitle: A reservable event setting inside Bossone Enterprise Research Center
cards.notes: This patio is useful when a recognized student organization wants an outdoor setting and is prepared to use Drexel’s event-request process.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor outdoor patio documented as a University City event space.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel lists the third-floor outdoor patio in Bossone Enterprise Research Center among its University City campus event spaces.
cards.access_notes: This is an event space, not an unrestricted public patio; recognized student organizations submit reservation requests through DragonLink.

cards.title: Plan Volleyball or an Outdoor Cookout
cards.subtitle: A campus recreation area with a court and barbecue
cards.notes: The documented amenities suit an outdoor recreation break or an organized gathering, subject to the applicable reservation process.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus area equipped with a volleyball court and barbecue.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel identifies Buckley Green as an outdoor recreation area with a barbecue and volleyball court on the University City campus.
cards.access_notes: Organized events and exclusive use require the applicable campus reservation process; observe posted rules.

cards.title: Give the Project Team a Door and a Screen
cards.subtitle: Twenty-two rooms sized for groups of four to twelve
cards.notes: Reserve one when a group needs a writing surface or wall-mounted monitor rather than an open table.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms designed for small and medium-sized group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel Libraries says Hagerty Library has 22 group study rooms for four to 12 people, each with a writing surface or wall-mounted monitor.
cards.access_notes: Limited to current Drexel students, faculty, and staff with University ID; groups of at least two may reserve up to three hours.

cards.title: Use a Zone Built Into the After-Hours Study Mix
cards.subtitle: A named practice area among booths, tables, and group-work options
cards.notes: Choose this area when practice work fits the task, with nearby seating formats available for switching between individual and group activity.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated Practice Zone within the Learning Den’s varied study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel Libraries identifies a Practice Zone among the 24-hour Learning Den’s booths, tables, and group-work options.
cards.access_notes: Available to the Drexel community; Dragon Card swipe entry is required after Hagerty Library closes.

cards.title: Know the Tech Lounge by Name
cards.subtitle: A designated space in the Creese–MacAlister student-center complex
cards.notes: Treat it as a campus-community option to check when you need a technology-oriented lounge; the source does not document its equipment or availability.
cards.short_summary: A named Tech Lounge within Drexel’s central student-center complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel lists a Tech Lounge among the services and spaces in the Creese Student Center and MacAlister Hall complex.
cards.access_notes: Campus-community space; the source does not state equipment, reservation rules, or hours, so check locally before relying on access.

cards.title: Meet on the Grass Without Booking a Room
cards.subtitle: A 2.5-acre recreational green shared with Powelton Village
cards.notes: Use the open green for recreation, relaxation, or an informal meetup while respecting any scheduled activity occupying part of the park.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge green serving both Drexel and the surrounding community.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel describes Drexel Park as a 2.5-acre recreational green space serving the university and Powelton Village communities.
cards.access_notes: Shared outdoor green space; scheduled activities may occupy portions of it, and posted rules apply.

warnings: Hours, room availability, event reservations, and building-entry rules can change; consult the cited Drexel pages or posted notices before relying on access.
Coordinates and map links are location aids from the supplied research dossier; the cited Drexel sources support the editorial claims.
